breaking_news.headline: Computer scientist on why he believes mass layoffs due to AI is a 'convenient excuse'
breaking_news.summary: NPR's Steve Inskeep asks Princeton computer scientist Sayash Kapoor about his assertions that AI won't lead to mass layoffs.

breaking_news.headline: How to eat out without spending a fortune
breaking_news.summary: Personal finance and nutrition experts share simple strategies that make it possible to eat out on a budget. One tip? You might have to let go of your fast food delivery habit.

breaking_news.headline: Meta considered buying Kalshi before developing its own prediction market app
breaking_news.summary: Mark Zuckerberg met with Kalshi's CEO last year about a potential deal, but talks did not move forward. Now Meta is making its own prediction market app.

breaking_news.headline: U.S. job market slows in June
breaking_news.summary: Employers added 57,000 jobs in June, the Labor Department said on Friday, as jobs growth slowed from the previous two months, while the unemployment rate ticked down to 4.2%.

breaking_news.headline: Trump earned more than $1 billion from crypto — but his investors didn't fare so well
breaking_news.summary: President Trump earned more than $1 billion in 2025 from cryptocurrency ventures. But there are thousands of investors who bought into some of those cryptocurrencies, and they stand to lose big.

breaking_news.headline: A hot summer trend in the sharing economy? Rental swimming pools
breaking_news.summary: Don't have a pool during this hot summer? Rent one! Swimply is a platform that lets users rent private pools.

breaking_news.headline: A hot summer trend in the sharing economy? Rental swimming pools
breaking_news.summary: The Airbnb-style company Swimply said there have been about 275,000 private pool reservations so far this year.

breaking_news.headline: But first, coffee: The drink that energized the American Revolution
breaking_news.summary: Colonial Americans were drinking coffee long before they dumped tea into Boston Harbor or fought a war for independence. The establishments that served it were already brewing revolutionary ideas.

breaking_news.headline: Ukrainian suspect hunted by police after Monaco bomb attack was 'disguised as a man'
breaking_news.summary: Officials believe the suspect may not have acted alone and spent days casing out the scene of the attack.

breaking_news.headline: Pope urges Europe to do more for migrants while visiting gateway island
breaking_news.summary: The pontiff pays tribute to migrants who lost their lives at sea at a cemetery on the Italian island of Lampedusa.

breaking_news.headline: 'Flamingo Revolution' takes off as thousands demand Albanian PM's resignation
breaking_news.summary: Flamingos have become a national symbol of protest, triggered by opposition to a luxury development.

breaking_news.headline: Anguished families left to identify Venezuela quake victims at makeshift morgue
breaking_news.summary: The disaster has overwhelmed local services, with bodies put outside or in tents for identification.

breaking_news.headline: Large crowds gather in Tehran on first day of Ayatollah Khamenei's funeral
breaking_news.summary: Ali Khamenei's body will lie in state in Tehran's Grand Mosalla until Monday, before travelling across Iran and Iraq.

breaking_news.headline: Keiko Fujimori declared winner of Peru's presidential election weeks after vote
breaking_news.summary: The daughter of disgraced president Alberto Fujimori is declared winner of tight race nearly a month after voting took place.

breaking_news.headline: Brutal heat cancels Fourth of July events, from DC to Philadelphia
breaking_news.summary: More than 165 million people are enduring dangerous heat and humidity, with temperatures expected to stay at 38C (100F) for several days.

breaking_news.headline: Taylor Swift marries Travis Kelce in NYC ceremony officiated by Adam Sandler
breaking_news.summary: The star-studded celebration saw several streets in Midtown Manhattan shut, as hordes of fans gathered outside the arena.

breaking_news.headline: Instagram running ads promoting child sexual abuse material in India, BBC finds
breaking_news.summary: The ads use terms including “rape” and “child video” and link to content on the messaging app Telegram.

breaking_news.headline: 'Less than 10% sheep': How millions may have unknowingly eaten goat, skin and fat kebabs
breaking_news.summary: Millions are likely to have eaten "lamb" kebabs that were actually made with goat, skin and fat.

breaking_news.headline: AI is 'not smart' so what's next in artificial intelligence?
breaking_news.summary: Leading AI researcher Yan LeCun has a start-up which is developing a more flexible AI system.

breaking_news.headline: Pubs allowed to stay open until 5am on Monday for England Mexico match
breaking_news.summary: The government had initially said it would not relax licensing laws further for the World Cup.
